statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 12% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both instruments. Conditional risk is concentrated in a narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs, where the published forecast reaches the WATCH band for two hours. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Record Nasdaq-100 close, balanced overnight tape and a compressing VIX keep Tail in the low band
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40, up 0.82% and 38 points below its 30,770.63 session high, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 range, completing its first record close since June alongside a second consecutive record Nasdaq Composite close. Globex NQ trades at 31,028, unchanged on the session, inside a 72-point overnight band of 30,997.50-31,070.00 and near its midpoint, so no persistent one-way structure, shallow-pullback sequence or failed-retracement pattern has been observed since the reopen. VIX at 14.21 is down 4.4% and settled near its 14.19 session low, while the 10-year Treasury yield held at 4.968%, up half a basis point, against a 2-year of 4.76%. WTI at $90.19 and Brent at $99.17 extended a sixth consecutive decline after Iran signalled it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and Saudi Aramco restarted its East-West pipeline, an easing of the energy shock that has supported growth-equity valuations. Cross-asset internals are supportive but narrow rather than uniformly aligned: latest-session semiconductor performance was positive across all seven tracked names, averaging about +2.1%, while megacaps were split four up and four down and Communication Services lagged. That divergence, an elevated yield backdrop with the Fed having raised rates into an energy shock, and an unresolved Iran situation that includes a scheduled UN General Assembly address keep Stress in the moderate band. None of it constitutes observed evidence of a price path that denies mean reversion, so Tail stays at 12%.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a previously published Claude assessment. Tail ranged from 11% to 21%, with the mapped state EA_ON in 21 hours and WATCH in three: the 14:00 UTC cash-open hour and the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour block on 22 September. Stress peaked at 46% around the cash open and decayed to 35% by the 00:00 UTC slot as the record close was absorbed, while Confidence held between 84% and 88% throughout. The dominant mode ran as normal through the Asian and European hours, then shifted to trend-up after the U.S. open and stayed there into the overnight session. No past assessment has been restated using later information.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are expected to remain in the low Tail band through the Asian and European sessions, with conditional risk concentrated in the 13:30-15:00 UTC block where the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs coincide. Two forecast hours reach the WATCH band on the scenario of an opening-auction continuation leg that denies an early retracement, and both decay quickly once price discovery is orderly, because published Tail is scored down as soon as retracements are observed. A modest power-hour uptick reflects late-session continuation risk after a record close, and scores return to the overnight baseline once the cash session ends. Stress stays inside the moderate band throughout, carried by an elevated yield backdrop, narrow semiconductor leadership and an unresolved Iran situation rather than by any observed breakdown in mean reversion.
